back: To speak quietly and unclearly (negative association).
To speak in a quiet, low voice (can be positive, like murmur approval).
To speak louder (can indicate anger or hearing difficulties).
To speak very loudly (can convey urgency, anger, or frustration).
To make a very loud and high-pitched noise.
To speak or laugh with a very loud, deep sound (like a lion).
To talk continuously and in a light-hearted way.
To criticize someone's faults or duties continuously.
To talk about other people, often spreading rumours.
To argue in an irritated way about unimportant things.
Informal: To criticize someone, especially behind their back.
To say nice things to someone to get a favour (negative association).
Informal: To complain in an annoying way.
Speech problems involving abnormal pauses or repetition of sounds.
Being unable to say what you want to say (e.g., due to nervousness).
